name: parcels
description: Stage 3 private-parcel boundaries: GEOMETRY ONLY (apn/county/acres/st/use), no owner names or addresses ever. Phase 1 = clean-license statewide states per docs/research/2026-08-09-free-parcel-boundaries.md §6 (app repo).

parcels.apn: assessor parcel number / parcel ID (string), optional
parcels.county: county DISPLAY NAME (string), optional — T-0009 contract: numeric and letter codes are translated in normalize (FL CO_NO, VA FIPS, MD JURSCODE, NH CountyId, IN FIPS static tables; MT/TX remapped to their sources' name columns) and untranslatable codes are DROPPED, never shipped. NAMING CONVENTION: VA keeps its 'County'/'city' suffixes (Fairfax County vs Fairfax city are different places); every other state ships the bare name — the client must NEVER append ' County' itself
parcels.acres: source-published acreage rounded to 2 decimals (number), optional — NEVER computed from geometry in v1. Source reality (2026-10 probe): absent at source in UT/VA/ME, WI GISACRES unconfirmed on the current vintage, ~96% null in OH; normalize prints per-attribute null rates so field-name drift is visible in CI
parcels.use: normalized land-use bucket (string), optional — one of RES AG VAC COM IND FOREST GOV; v1 states (6) FL MA IN DC WI MT; adapters normalize assessment classes in the pipeline and the client maps buckets to labels (app USE_LABELS — change only in lockstep). Excluded after live probes 2026-10-25: TX (field unpopulated), CT (municipal code soup), MD (desc field empty), VT (field is parcel-kind), HI (zoning-district). NJ dropped post-run-40243912707: PROP_CLASS is on the MOD-IV composite service, not the statewide gdb (FGDB -select hard-fails on unknown names); NJ's future use route is that service.

schema.contract_note: This schema is the CONTRACT with the Android client (parcel identify sheet). It is also the QA WHITELIST: qa_parcels.py hard-fails the build if any other attribute key reaches the normalized output or a decoded tile. Owner names/addresses in tiles would convert a $0 layer into a vendor licensing negotiation — the whitelist gate is the enforcement point (research §5, §6 risk 4). It also neutralizes MT MCA 2-6-1017 and ID §74-120 mailing-list statutes.
schema.shards_note: Unit codes in sources.json are state codes, sharded states use ST_1/ST_2 (TX, FL); st = unit prefix. Shards split on FILE LISTS, never attribute where-clauses: TX by FIPS range over mirrored county zips, FL by size-balanced halves of the FDOR county-zip list (attribute filters against the FL AGOL service are unindexed/504-prone — see sources.json FL_1 notes).

sources: layers/parcels/sources.json — one entry per matrix unit: {mode: http|rest, urls, layer, fields{apn,county,acres}, use_field? + use_adapter? (T-0012, set both or neither), where?, count_expected, notes}. Endpoints + field names live-verified 2026-08-09. License basis per state: app repo docs/research/2026-08-09-free-parcel-boundaries.md §2 — do not add a state that is not CONFIRMED/clean there without founder sign-off.

qa.attribute_whitelist: HARD GATE (qa_parcels.py): every feature in parcels.geojsonl AND in decoded sample tiles must carry ONLY keys ⊆ {apn, county, acres, st, use}. Any other key fails the build. This is the owner-names-never-in-tiles invariant.
qa.use_vocabulary: HARD GATE (qa_parcels.py, T-0012), beside the whitelist gate in the same two places — the Gate 1 full geojsonl scan AND the Gate 3 decoded-tile loop: any feature whose use value is not one of {RES, AG, VAC, COM, IND, FOREST, GOV} fails the build ('use vocabulary violation: <value>'). An absent use is fine (optional); a present out-of-vocabulary one is not. One shared constant (qa_parcels.USE_BUCKETS) must equal normalize_parcels.USE_BUCKETS and the app's USE_LABELS — change all three in lockstep.
qa.count: kept feature count within tolerance (default ±25%) of sources.json count_expected (vintages drift annually)
qa.size_calibration: KB/parcel printed per unit; expected 0.4-0.7 KB/parcel through the pyramid (research §5, calibrated vs lands). WARN outside 0.2-1.5 — the pilot (UT MT WI) validates the constant before the full matrix is trusted.

pilot: Per research §5 risk control: UT + MT + WI first (workflow_dispatch states subset, artifact-only), check KB/parcel constant, then full matrix.
